question_text: When a concave mirror of focal length $f$ is immersed in water, its focal length becomes $f'$, then
options: The information is insufficient to predict
solution: The focal length of a spherical mirror depends only on its radius of curvature ($f = R/2$) and is independent of the refractive index of the surrounding medium. Therefore, when immersed in water, its focal length remains unchanged, i.e., $f' = f$.

question_text: A person cannot see objects clearly that are closer than $2\text{ m}$ and farther than $4\text{ m}$. To correct the eye vision, the person will use
options: Bifocal lenses of power $-3.5\text{ D}$ and $0.25\text{ D}$
Bifocal lenses of power $-0.25\text{ D}$ and $3.5\text{ D}$
Bifocal lenses of power $-0.5\text{ D}$ and $4.0\text{ D}$
Bifocal lenses of power $-4.0\text{ D}$ and $0.5\text{ D}$
solution:
For distant vision (myopia correction), the far point is at $v = -4	ext{ m}$ for an object at $u = -\infty$. Thus, $P_1 =  rac{1}{f_1} =  rac{1}{-4} = -0.25	ext{ D}$.
For near vision (hypermetropia correction), to see an object at standard near point $u = -25	ext{ cm} = -0.25	ext{ m}$ at the defective near point $v = -2	ext{ m}$:
$P_2 =  rac{1}{f_2} =  rac{1}{v} -  rac{1}{u} = - rac{1}{2} - \left(- rac{1}{0.25}ight) = -0.5 + 4 = +3.5	ext{ D}$.
Hence, bifocal lenses of power $-0.25	ext{ D}$ and $3.5	ext{ D}$ are required.

question_text: Minimum distance between real object and image produced by a concave mirror of focal length $20\text{ cm}$ is
solution: When a real object is placed at the center of curvature of a concave mirror ($u = 2f$), its real image is also formed at the center of curvature ($v = 2f$). Thus, the distance between the object and image is zero, which is the minimum possible distance.

question_text: An object is at a distance of $30\text{ cm}$ in front of a concave mirror of focal length $10\text{ cm}$. The image of the object will be
options: Between focus and centre of curvature
solution: Here, $f = -10\text{ cm}$ and $R = 20\text{ cm}$. The object is placed at $u = -30\text{ cm}$, which is beyond the center of curvature ($u > 2f$).\nUsing the mirror formula: $\frac{1}{v} = \frac{1}{f} - \frac{1}{u} = -\frac{1}{10} + \frac{1}{30} = -\frac{1}{15} \implies v = -15\text{ cm}$.\nSince $10\text{ cm} < |v| < 20\text{ cm}$, the image is formed between focus and center of curvature. Magnification $m = -\frac{v}{u} = -\frac{-15}{-30} = -0.5$, which means the image is real, inverted, and smaller in size (diminished). Thus, all statements are correct.

question_text: In normal adjustment the angular magnification of an astronomical telescope is $39$. If length of the tube is $2\text{ m}$, then focal length of the objective and eyepiece are respectively
solution:
In normal adjustment of an astronomical telescope:
$m =  rac{f_o}{f_e} = 39 \implies f_o = 39f_e$
Tube length $L = f_o + f_e = 2	ext{ m} = 200	ext{ cm}$
$39f_e + f_e = 200 \implies 40f_e = 200 \implies f_e = 5	ext{ cm}$
$f_o = 39 	imes 5 = 195	ext{ cm}$.

question_text: A convex lens of focal length $10\text{ cm}$ forms real image of an object. The distance between the object and the image may be
solution: For a real object and a real image formed by a convex lens, the minimum separation between the object and image is $D_{\min} = 4f$.\nGiven $f = 10\text{ cm}$, we have $D_{\min} = 4 \times 10 = 40\text{ cm}$.\nTherefore, the distance between the object and image must be $D \ge 40\text{ cm}$. Among the given choices, only $50\text{ cm}$ satisfies this condition.

question_text: A plano-convex lens of focal length $20\text{ cm}$ is silver painted on its plane face, as shown. The distance of the image of object $\text{O}$ from the lens-mirror system is
diagram_description: A plano-convex lens with its plane surface silvered. An object O is situated on the principal axis facing the curved surface at a distance of 10 cm from the lens.
solution:
The effective power of the silvered lens system is:
$P = 2P_L + P_M \implies  rac{1}{F} =  rac{2}{f_L} +  rac{1}{f_M}$
Here $f_L = 20	ext{ cm}$ and for the flat silvered surface, $f_M = \infty$.
$ rac{1}{F} =  rac{2}{20} + 0 =  rac{1}{10}	ext{ cm}^{-1} \implies F = 10	ext{ cm}$.
The silvered lens behaves as an equivalent concave mirror of focal length $F = 10	ext{ cm}$.
Since the object is placed at $u = 10	ext{ cm}$, it lies exactly at the principal focus of the system. Hence, the image is formed at infinity.
